chapter.name: Anti-Defection Provisions
chapter.blurb: The Tenth Schedule, its grounds and exceptions, the deciding authority, the 91st Amendment and key Supreme Court rulings.

91st Amendment, case law, disqualification table, key numbers

concepts.name: Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) and the 91st Amendment
concepts.description: Origin, grounds, exceptions, whip, deciding authority, 91st Amendment changes, case law and key numbers.
concepts.idea: The Tenth Schedule disqualifies defectors, with merger and presiding-officer exceptions, decided by the presiding officer under judicial review.
concepts.rule: The Tenth Schedule, inserted by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Articles 102(2) and 191(2)), disqualifies a legislator who voluntarily gives up party membership (conduct counts) or defies the whip unless the party condones within 15 days; an independent who joins a party and a nominated member who joins after six months are also disqualified. Exceptions are a merger agreed by two-thirds of the party and the presiding-officer exemption; the one-third split exemption was deleted by the 91st Amendment, 2003. The Speaker or Chairman decides (a member elected by the House if he is the subject), subject to judicial review after Kihoto Hollohan (1992); the Court in 2020 asked for decisions within three months. The 91st Amendment also capped Councils of Ministers at 15 per cent (States not below 12) and barred disqualified defectors from ministerial office.
concepts.example: A nominated member who joins a party four months after taking his seat is not disqualified.

questions.q: Besides inserting the Tenth Schedule, the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 made changes in four Articles of the Constitution, all dealing with vacation of seats and disqualification of legislators. These Articles are
questions.e: Perthe amended Articles are 101, 102, 190 and 191; the disqualification on defection is anchored in Article 102(2) for Parliament and 191(2) for State Legislatures.
w: Articles 103 and 192 only give the decision on certain disqualifications to the President/Governor; they are not the amended ones.
Articles 100 and 189 deal with voting and quorum and were not amended.
Articles 84 and 173 deal with qualifications for membership and were not amended.

questions.q: A person nominated to the Rajya Sabha takes his seat on 1 March and joins a political party on 15 July of the same year. Under the Tenth Schedule he
questions.a: is not disqualified, because he joined within six months of taking his seat
o: is not disqualified, because he joined within six months of taking his seat
is disqualified, because a nominated member may never join a party after nomination
is disqualified, because the grace period for a nominated member is only three months
is disqualified unless the Chairman of the House permits him to join the party
questions.e: A nominated member is disqualified only if he joins a party after six months from taking his seat. 1 March to 15 July is under six months; the window lets him decide his alignment while preventing later opportunistic switching.
w: The bar applies only to a joining after six months, not to any joining.
The period is six months, not three.
No permission of the Chairman is part of the rule; the six-month window decides it.

questions.q: A legislator elected on a party ticket abstains from a vote in disobedience of the party whip, without prior permission. His disqualification can be averted if the party condones the act within
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule saves the member if the party condones the whip violation within 15 days. Abstaining is treated like voting against.
w: 30 days is not the period in the Schedule.
7 days is not the period in the Schedule.
60 days is the absence limit for vacating a seat, a different rule.

questions.q: Which one of the following provisions of the Tenth Schedule did the Supreme Court declare unconstitutional in Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992)?
questions.a: The clause making the presiding officer's decision immune from court review
o: The clause making the presiding officer's decision immune from court review
The disqualification of a member who votes against his party's direction
The exemption from disqualification on a merger agreed by two-thirds of members
The vesting of the power to decide defection cases in the presiding officer
questions.e: The Court upheld the Schedule but struck down the finality clause (para 7) because it took away the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts; the presiding officer acts as a tribunal and is subject to judicial review.
w: The whip ground was upheld.
The merger exception was not struck down.
The Court rejected the objection that vesting adjudication in the presiding officer is invalid for political bias.

questions.q: According to the Supreme Court in Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur (2020), a presiding officer should ordinarily decide a disqualification petition under the Tenth Schedule within
questions.e: The Court (2020) fixed an outer limit of three months barring extraordinary circumstances; the Act itself, asrecords, prescribes no time limit.
w: Not the period fixed.
Not the period fixed; six months is the nominated-member window.
Not the period fixed.
tr: Time limit not in the Act

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the anti-defection law in India:

1. It was brought in by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985, which inserted the Tenth Schedule.
2. Its disqualification provisions bind Members of Parliament, while members of State Legislatures are covered by separate laws made by each State.
3. One of its aims is to keep elected governments stable by curbing defections prompted by personal gain.
4. It was a response to the political instability of the 1960s and 1970s, when frequent floor-crossing earned the label 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram'.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Schedule was inserted in 1985. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 191(2) applies the same Tenth Schedule to State legislators. Statement 3 is correct: stability and party discipline are the stated aims. Statement 4 is correct: that is the mischief addressed.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification under the Tenth Schedule:

1. A member elected on a party ticket can incur disqualification for voluntarily giving up membership even without a formal resignation, if his conduct shows he has quit (as read in Ravi S. Naik, 1994).
2. An independent member who joins a political party after being elected is disqualified.
3. An independent member may extend outside support to a government without attracting disqualification, so long as he does not join a party.
4. Rules made by the presiding officer to give effect to the Tenth Schedule take effect without having to be placed before the House.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: conduct counts. Statement 2 is correct: that is a Tenth Schedule ground. Statement 3 is correct: disqualification arises on joining. Statement 4 is incorrect: such rules must be placed before the House for 30 days, and the House may approve, modify or disapprove them.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the whip:

1. The whip system originated in the American Congress and was adopted in India from there.
2. The term whip denotes both a party's written direction to legislators on voting and the party officer who coordinates members on the floor.
3. The post of whip owes its existence to parliamentary convention, since neither the Constitution nor the Rules of the House provide for it.
4. Political parties, whether ruling or in opposition, can issue whips to their legislators.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it originated in British parliamentary practice. Statement 2 is correct: both senses. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct: every party has its whips.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the exceptions to disqualification on the ground of defection:

1. A merger of a party is protected once a simple majority of its legislators agree to it.
2. A member elected Speaker or Chairman may give up his party membership and rejoin it after leaving the office without incurring disqualification.
3. The presiding officer's exemption was provided in view of the dignity and impartiality of the office.
4. Even after the 91st Amendment, a split by one-third of a legislature party is protected as an exception alongside merger.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: two-thirds must agree. Statement 2 is correct: presiding-officer exemption. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the split exemption was deleted in 2003.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about who decides questions of disqualification:

1. Questions of disqualification on the ground of defection are decided by the Speaker or the Chairman of the House concerned, and not by the President or the Governor.
2. For grounds listed in Articles 102 and 191, such as an office of profit or being an undischarged insolvent, the President (Governor for State legislators) decides after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion.
3. If the complaint is against the Speaker himself, it is decided by the Election Commission on a reference from the House.
4. Vesting the decision in the presiding officer is criticised because he may not act impartially, being himself a party member, and may lack the legal training to adjudicate.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under the Tenth Schedule defection disqualification is decided by the Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned, not by the President or Governor. Statement 2 is correct: for the grounds in Articles 102 and 191 the President (Governor for State legislators) decides after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion, as Articles 103 and 192 provide. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Election Commission has no such role under the Tenth Schedule; such a complaint goes to a member elected by the House for the purpose. Statement 4 is correct: the presiding officer belongs to a party and has no legal training, which are the two standard criticisms.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: the Speaker or Chairman decides defection cases.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: partisanship and lack of legal training are the standard criticisms.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: the Election Commission does not decide a complaint against the Speaker.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the changes made by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003:

1. It removed the exemption that had protected a split by one-third of a legislature party.
2. A legislator disqualified for defection cannot be appointed a minister until his House's term ends or he is re-elected, whichever is earlier.
3. The Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, can be no larger than 15 per cent of the strength of the Lok Sabha.
4. After 2003 a merger agreed by two-thirds of the legislature party is the only group arrangement that protects members who leave their party.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: only merger remains. Statement 2 is correct: Articles 75(1B)/164(1B). Statement 3 is correct: Article 75(1A). Statement 4 is correct: merger remains the sole protected route.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the size of Councils of Ministers:

1. In a State, the Council of Ministers including the Chief Minister may not exceed 15 per cent of the strength of the Assembly.
2. The minimum size of a State's Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is fixed at 7 in every State by the 91st Amendment.
3. The ceiling on the Union Council of Ministers is 15 per cent of the combined strength of both Houses of Parliament.
4. Until 2003 the Constitution limited the Council of Ministers to 10 per cent of the House, a limit the 91st Amendment raised to 15 per cent.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 164(1A); the floor is 12. Statement 2 is incorrect: the 91st Amendment fixes the minimum at 12, not 7; only some smaller States have a lower floor, so 7 is not the rule in every State. Statement 3 is incorrect: it is 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is incorrect: there was no cap earlier; 10 per cent was only an NCRWC recommendation.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the anti-defection law and the Supreme Court:

1. Under the rules made for the Tenth Schedule, the presiding officer can take up a defection case only on a complaint from a member of the House, and must first let the accused member explain.
2. In Ravi S. Naik (1994) the Court held that only a formal resignation from the party amounts to voluntarily giving up membership.
3. In G. Vishwanathan (1996) the Court held that a member expelled by his party ceases to belong to it for Tenth Schedule purposes.
4. Two Speakers of the Lok Sabha have themselves expressed doubts about their suitability to adjudicate defection cases.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the presiding officer acts only on a member's complaint and after hearing the accused. Statement 2 is incorrect: conduct can show voluntary giving up (Ravi S. Naik, 1994). Statement 3 is incorrect: an expelled member continues to belong to the party (G. Vishwanathan, 1996). Statement 4 is correct: Rabi Ray (1991) and Shivraj Patil (1993).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification of members of legislatures:

1. A person holding any office of profit under the Union or a State Government is disqualified from Parliament even if the office is that of a Minister.
2. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a conviction resulting in imprisonment of two years or more is a ground of disqualification.
3. Failure to lodge an account of election expenses within time is a ground under the Tenth Schedule.
4. A House may declare a seat vacant if a member is absent from all meetings for sixty days without permission, ignoring periods when it is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 102 exempts offices that Parliament has declared not to disqualify, and Union and State ministerial offices are so exempted, so a Minister is not disqualified. Statement 2 is correct: under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 conviction with imprisonment of two years or more disqualifies. Statement 3 is incorrect: failure to lodge an account of election expenses is a ground under the Representation of the People Act, not the Tenth Schedule. Statement 4 is correct: under Article 101(4) the House may declare the seat vacant after sixty days' absence, not counting periods of prorogation or adjournment for more than four consecutive days.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the RP Act disqualifies on conviction with two years or more.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: Ministers are exempted from the office-of-profit bar.
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the RP Act disqualifies on conviction with two years or more.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the working of the Tenth Schedule:

1. A member who abstains from a vote contrary to his party's direction, without prior permission and without condonation, is liable to disqualification just like one who votes against it.
2. Once a member breaches the party direction, disqualification takes effect on its own, without any complaint or hearing.
3. Before taking a decision, the presiding officer may refer the complaint to the Committee of Privileges for inquiry.
4. A member elected on a party ticket who joins another party escapes disqualification unless he first resigns his seat in the House.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Tenth Schedule disqualifies a member who votes or abstains contrary to the party direction without prior permission or condonation. Statement 2 is incorrect: disqualification is not automatic; the presiding officer acts only on a member's complaint after hearing the accused. Statement 3 is correct: the presiding officer may refer the complaint to the Committee of Privileges before deciding. Statement 4 is incorrect: joining another party is itself voluntarily giving up membership, so resignation is not needed to attract disqualification. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 91st Amendment Act, 2003:

1. It made several changes in the Tenth Schedule itself, including inserting the exemption for mergers.
2. The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) recommended that the exemption for splits be retained.
3. The NCRWC (2002) recommended the same 15 per cent ceiling on ministers that the Amendment adopted.
4. It bars a disqualified defector from appointment as a minister but leaves him free to hold remunerative political posts.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it made one change, omitting the split exemption; merger was already there. Statement 2 is incorrect: it recommended omission, as did the Law Commission (1999) and the NCRWC (2002). Statement 3 is incorrect: the NCRWC recommended 10 per cent. Statement 4 is incorrect: he is also disqualified from remunerative political posts. So exactly 0 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 0 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 0 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 0 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992):

1. The clause making the presiding officer's decision final and immune from courts was declared unconstitutional.
2. The Court held that the presiding officer acts as a legislative authority, so his decision cannot be examined on grounds such as mala fides.
3. The Court struck down the Tenth Schedule as a whole for violating the freedom of conscience of legislators.
4. The Court held that vesting adjudication in the presiding officer is invalid because of political bias.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: it took away court jurisdiction. Statement 2 is incorrect: he acts as a tribunal; review lies for mala fides, perversity etc. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Court upheld the Tenth Schedule and struck down only the finality clause. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Court rejected that contention. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A nominated member of a House may join a political party within six months of taking his seat without being disqualified.
Statement-II: A member who is elected the presiding officer of a House and gives up his party membership is not disqualified.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is also correct but concerns presiding officers, not the nominated-member window, so it does not explain Statement-I.
w: Statement-II concerns presiding officers, not nominated members or the six-month window, so it cannot explain it.
Statement-II is correct, so this rejects a true statement.
Statement-I is correct, so this rejects a true statement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The office of whip is not mentioned in the Constitution.
Statement-II: A member who votes or abstains contrary to his party's whip, without permission or condonation, can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is also correct (Tenth Schedule), but the penalty for defying a whip does not explain why the Constitution omits the office.
w: Statement-II concerns the consequence of defiance, not the absence of the office from the Constitution, so it is not the reason.
Statement-II is correct, so it is not incorrect.
Statement-I is correct (the Constitution does not mention the whip).

questions.q:
Match each Supreme Court ruling on the anti-defection law in List-I with the principle it laid down in List-II.

List-I
A. Kihoto Hollohan (1992)
B. Ravi S. Naik (1994)
C. G. Vishwanathan (1996)
D. Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020)

List-II
1. Expelled member continues to belong to the original party
2. Voluntary giving up of membership can be inferred from conduct
3. Tenth Schedule held constitutionally valid
4. Petitions ordinarily to be decided within three months
questions.e: Kihoto: Tenth Schedule held constitutionally valid; Ravi Naik: conduct; Vishwanathan: expelled member remains in party; Meghachandra: three months.
w: A and B are interchanged.
C and D are interchanged.
A and C are interchanged.
